chain.label: SWA guidance/training gap on braking reports and landing distance assumptions
chain.trigger: Southwest Airlines did not provide its pilots with clear and consistent guidance and training regarding company policies and procedures in several areas, including interpretation of braking action reports and the assumptions affecting landing distance assessments.

chain.label: OPC concealed non-conservative assumptions and carried no safety margin
chain.trigger: the landing distances displayed on the OPC could have been misleading to the crew because the pilots were not aware of at least two underlying OPC assumptions, neither of which was displayed on the OPC... Both of these assumptions resulted in OPC indications showing larger (more favorable) stopping margins.

chain.label: first-ever autobrake landing; policy implemented with no familiarization period
chain.trigger: the accident landing was the first time either pilot landed using autobrakes... At the time of the accident, SWA's planned implementation of its autobrakes procedures did not include a familiarization period.

caused_by.evidence: feedback from other SWA pilots should have alerted SWA management and the company's FAA POI to the need for a familiarization or transition period.

chain.label: substandard runway 31C safety area with no EMAS installed
chain.trigger: the runway 31C RSA extended 82 feet beyond the end of the runway and was 500 feet wide... no such improvements had been made when the accident occurred.

chain.label: snow-contaminated runway 31C, mixed braking action with poor on second half
chain.trigger: continue for [runway] 31C the winds zero nine zero at nine, brakin' action reported good for the first half, poor for the second half.

chain.label: 8-knot tailwind component, above the 5-knot poor-braking limit
chain.trigger: The reported wind conditions resulted in a computed tailwind component of 8 knots... SWA policies... do not authorize landings on runways with more than a 5-knot tailwind component with poor braking action.

chain.label: crew did not use the most critical braking term (poor) in the arrival assessment
chain.trigger: because the pilots did not use the more critical braking action term (poor) during their landing distance assessment (which, combined with the associated tailwind limitation, would have required them to divert), they were not in compliance with SWA's policies.

caused_by.evidence: All of the braking action reports provided by ATC to the accident pilots were mixed and reported poor braking action on some portion of the runway.
the topic of mixed conditions was not routinely introduced to pilots during training and was absent in the FOM for the topics of braking action and runway friction reports

chain.label: decision to land at MDW rather than divert to an alternate
chain.trigger: Also contributing to the accident was the pilots' failure to divert to another airport given reports that included poor braking action and a tailwind component greater than 5 knots.

caused_by.evidence: the pilots evaluated and discussed performance calculations for both fair and poor reported braking conditions... their behavior and other discussion suggests that they interpreted the runway condition as closer to fair than poor

if the pilots had been presented with stopping margins associated with the input winds or had known that the stopping margins calculated by the OPC for the 737-700 already assumed credit for the use of thrust reversers, the pilots may have elected to divert
the tailwind component exceeded the 5-knot limit for poor runway conditions, but the displayed stopping margin was instead based on the tailwind limit of 5 knots

chain.label: crew attention absorbed by unfamiliar autobrake system after touchdown
chain.trigger: He told investigators that he believed that the use of the autobrake system distracted his attention from the thrust reversers after his initial attempt to deploy them.

caused_by.evidence: The pilots' first use of the airplane's autobrake system during a challenging landing situation led to the pilots' distraction from the otherwise routine task of deploying the thrust reversers promptly after touchdown.
they ultimately agreed that use of the autobrakes would allow them to stop in the shortest distance and used the autobrakes on maximum setting during the accident landing

Because of the pilots' concerns regarding the autobrakes and their unfamiliarity with the system's operation, it would have been natural for them to focus on the autobrake system's performance after the airplane touched down.

chain.label: reverse thrust not commanded until 15 seconds after touchdown
chain.trigger: The first indication of thrust reverser activity was recorded about 15 seconds after touchdown, with full deployment about 18 seconds after touchdown.

caused_by.evidence: the captain (the flying pilot) did not deploy reverse thrust immediately after the airplane touched down... his focus on the autobrake system performance distracted him from trying to deploy the thrust reversers again

chain.label: airplane departed the end of runway 31C at about 53 knots
chain.trigger: the airplane ran off the departure end of runway 31C and continued through the runway safety area (RSA), a blast fence, a navigational aid antenna, across an airport road, through an airport perimeter fence

caused_by.evidence: the pilots would have been able to stop the airplane on the runway if they had commanded maximum reverse thrust promptly after touchdown and maintained maximum reverse thrust to a full stop
the flight's braking ability was about five times worse than would be expected on a bare and dry runway

A simulation case performed under the same conditions but with an equivalent headwind instead of tailwind component... showed that the airplane could have stopped about 584 feet before the departure end of the runway.

chain.label: airplane left airport property and struck an automobile on the roadway
chain.trigger: The airplane struck a northbound automobile on that roadway before it came to rest near an intersection located on the northwest corner of the airport.

caused_by.evidence: onto an adjacent public roadway. The airplane struck a northbound automobile on that roadway

the absence of an EMAS installation in the limited overrun area for runway 31C contributed to the severity of the accident; even a nonstandard EMAS installation would have safely stopped the airplane before it left airport property

chain.label: one child killed, one serious and 21 minor injuries
chain.trigger: A child in the automobile was killed, one automobile occupant received serious injuries, and three other automobile occupants received minor injuries. Eighteen of the 103 airplane occupants... received minor injuries

caused_by.evidence: The Cook County Medical Examiner's Office reported the cause of death of the automobile passenger as 'compressional asphyxia.'
